Why It Matters: Anchors scope and success; every deliverable should trace back to a goal.
Example Question to Ask Customer: What business outcome do you need from this project in the next 6 to 12 months?
What does your current environment look like (tenant, licenses, key systems, where the data lives)?

Why It Matters: Defines what is delivered and drives hours and price.
Example Question to Ask Customer: Which workloads, sites, applications and user groups are in scope, and roughly how many users?

Why It Matters: Prevents scope creep and disputes later.
Example Question to Ask Customer: Is there anything you explicitly do not want included in this phase?

Why It Matters: Can change the design, timeline and approvals needed.
Example Question to Ask Customer: Are there compliance, data residency, or works council and union requirements we must follow?

Why It Matters: Sets the phase plan, staffing and milestones.
Example Question to Ask Customer: When do you want to start, and is there a hard deadline or event driving the date?

Why It Matters: Confirms the proposed offers fit and sizes the SOW.
Example Question to Ask Customer: What budget range have you set aside for this work?

Why It Matters: Identifies who signs and how long approval takes.
Example Question to Ask Customer: Who makes the final decision, and what approvals are needed to sign the SOW?

Why It Matters: Defines acceptance and how value will be measured.
Example Question to Ask Customer: How will you measure success at the end of the engagement?

Why It Matters: Customer effort is an assumption in every SOW.
Example Question to Ask Customer: Who will be our day-to-day contact, and which of your team members will be available to us?

Why It Matters: Surfaces blockers early and shapes the assumptions.
Example Question to Ask Customer: Are there other projects, vendors or dependencies that could affect this work?
